To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) trust management provides a useful compromise between the expressiveness and tractability of capability-based systems and the ease of revocation provided by traditional access control lists, (ii) the access control mechanisms at the core of trust management systems can be formally modeled and compared with other access control models using the state-transition approach, and (iii) the trust management access control mechanism is equivalent to the Lampson access control mechanism when capabilities are modeled as rows of the access matrix.

the trust management access control mechanism is more expressive than access control lists and that the trust management mechanism is a tractable compromise that provides the benefits of capability-based systems without their drawbacks.

(1) trust management is a tractable compromise that lies somewhere between the unrestricted capability passing of the capability-based model and the easy revocation of the access control list model and (2) trust management is equivalent to access control lists and a form of capabilities that is based on unforgeable references.

the state-transition approach is a useful tool for analyzing the core access control mechanism of a wide variety of systems, and that trust management systems provide a useful compromise between the capability and access control list models.
